ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, managers and material counterparties against: (i) PEP status under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Law of 12 November 2004, including national PEP databases; (ii) the consolidated EU financial sanctions list; (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated list; (iv) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists for US-dollar clearing compatibility; and (v) Interpol notices and adverse-media sources. Enhanced due diligence and senior management approval are required for any PEP or designated-person match; freezes are applied for any UN/EU/OFC designation match; suspicious transaction reports must be filed promptly with the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF), and all KYC/AML records retained for at least five years post-business-relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal at www.lbr.lu (RCS - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), with applications filed through the MyLBR / guichet.lu e-justice system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be rendered in Latin characters; Luxembourg accepts names in French, German or Luxembourgish and permits foreign-language names only when transliterated into Latin script for RCS recording; the legal form designation 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the suffix 'SCSp' is recommended and the RCS classification must identify the entity as a special limited partnership; the name must be distinctive, not misleading, and not contrary to Luxembourg public policy or international public order under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Bque (requires CSSF banking licence under the Law of 5 April 1993)
Fonds de placement, SICAV, SICAF, Investment Fund, FCP (requires CSSF authorization under the Law of 17 December 2010)
Etat, State, National, Luxembourg, Grand-Duché, Gouvernement (misleading official connotation requiring ministerial or ILNAS clearance)
Euro, EU, Union Européenne, European (reserved or misleading supranational tokens)
Université, University, Ecole, School (requires ministerial approval)
Trust, Holding, Groupe (sensitive finance tokens triggering enhanced scrutiny and proof of permissible use)
SA, SARL, SCA, SE (legal form designations reserved for other corporate forms and prohibited for SCSp names)
Chambre de Commerce, Bourse, Stock Exchange (regulated professional bodies or market operators)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The LBR issues a 'certificat négatif' (negative certificate) reserving the name for 60 days; no statutory extension exists, but the applicant may resubmit the identical name immediately upon expiry if still available. In case of rejection, the applicant may: (1) file a revised name application via MyLBR without penalty; (2) obtain a notarized waiver (renonciation) from the prior name or trademark holder and resubmit; (3) request a written reasoned decision from the LBR; (4) lodge an administrative appeal before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification pursuant to the amended Law of 7 November 1996 on the organization of the administrative courts, with mandatory legal counsel and a statement of grounds; and (5) where the refusal is based on an earlier registered distinct name, negotiate a coexistence agreement or modify the distinctive element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited. An SCSp may validly register at the office of a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation company; however, an operating export-distribution business requiring SWIFT TT and letter-of-credit banking rails, food-safety registration and VAT compliance cannot rely on a pure virtual mailbox. A licensed domiciliation address with a local registered agent, physical records, administrative substance and callable local representation is acceptable and commercially necessary.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated for an active goods-distribution entity: estimated 30-45% probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first 36 months, driven primarily by the Administration de la sécurité alimentaire (ASV) for food import/export hygiene and labelling, by the customs and excise authorities for goods movement controls, and by RCS/LBR business-register compliance checks; risk intensifies after VAT registration thresholds and upon first annual accounts filing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Articles 944-1 to 944-21 (société en commandite spéciale) together with Article 904 et seq. (commandite principles); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register, Article 16 et seq.; Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to the professions of artisan, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions, Articles 2-13 and 27-30; Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 on the hygiene of foodstuffs, Articles 5-6 and Annex II; amended Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments, Article 1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 19-21 Boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg; electronic filing portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (constitutive deed) of the SCSp executed by the partners, either notarised or under private signature, filed via the RCS electronic form; the registration particulars are published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital applies to an SCSp under Article 944-1 et seq. of the Law of 1915; contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement. No escrow account or paid-up capital certification is required because the SCSp lacks legal personality; contributions in cash, in kind or in industry become due upon call as contractually agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the subscribers hereby constitute a société en commandite spéciale (SCSp) under Articles 944-1 et seq. of the amended Law of 10 August 1915; (2) the capital contributions set out in the contribution schedule are approved and fully subscribed; (3) the registered office is fixed at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg; (4) the general partner is authorised to govern the partnership and [PROPOSED MANAGING PARTNER] is appointed managing partner with sole signature authority; (5) the managing partner is authorised, acting alone, to open financial accounts, file RCS declarations, apply for the business permit, the ALVA registration and all ancillary licences, and sign sale and supply contracts in the ordinary course of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers – online pre-registration module (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed names with the legal-form suffix SCSp / Société en commandite spéciale through the LBR portal. The registry verifies identity conflicts and distinctive character and reserves the accepted name. The reservation is evidenced by a name-availability record to be attached to the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Identity document or RCS extract of the general partner(s)
Signed power of attorney of the filer (if not a partner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or similarity, file two fresh alternatives; a written opinion of the RCS registrar may be requested, and a court appeal before the District Court of Luxembourg is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the constitutive deed and first partners' resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (optional) or the partners themselves by private deed; deed may be signed in Luxembourg or abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the acte constitutif containing the name, registered office, corporate purpose (export wholesale of pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot soup base), term, contribution schedule, and the powers of the general partner and managing partner. The first partners' resolution is appended. For the SCSp, no notarial formality is mandatory, but signatures must be authenticated for RCS purposes through a certified signature or qualified electronic identification.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first partners' resolution and contribution schedule
Certified copies of partners' identity documents
Proof of address and occupancy title for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed contains a defective clause, execute an amendatory deed (avenant) signed by all partners and refile; notarial re-execution cures authentication objections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des impôts (ADI) — the unified Luxembourg tax administration formed by the merger of the Administration des contributions directes and the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; competent for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, VAT, registration duties and withholding taxes. Electronic portal: MyGuichet.lu, ADI e-TVA and e-CDF online services; commercial and taxpayer registration through the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) at lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp partnership agreement and file the required extract, bylaws, authorized signatories, registered office address and identity of the general partner (associé commandité) with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu or an approved fiduciary; obtain the RCS registration number and the national matricule number. Step 2: Submit the VAT registration application to the ADI through the e-TVA portal or the MyGuichet company-creation workspace, attaching the RCS extract, proof of registered office, identity of managers and bank KYC documents; the ADI issues an 8-digit Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + eight digits) within approximately 10 business days. Step 3: Non-resident partners do not require a Luxembourg tax ID for entity formation; if the SCSp carries on commercial activity through a Luxembourg fixed place of business, the partners may trigger Luxembourg tax filing obligations. Step 4: There is no tax authorization or agrément for hotpot soup base distribution; however, a food-export health certificate from the Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (ALVA) may be required by the importing country.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is transparent for Luxembourg income taxes: it is not subject to corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) or net wealth tax (IF); income, gains and losses are allocated directly to the general and limited partners. For VAT, the SCSp is treated as an independent taxable person (assujetti) to the extent it makes economic supplies; the territorial scope of partner taxation depends on the partner's own residence, with non-resident partners exposed to Luxembourg tax only if the SCSp's activity constitutes a Luxembourg permanent establishment or fixed place of business for them.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp cannot elect to become opaque for income tax: the Article 175 LIR taxation option for partnerships is limited to entities in which all partners are indefinitely and jointly liable (in practice the SNC), a condition the SCSp cannot meet because limited partners (commanditaires) benefit from limited liability. Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime; the pass-through classification is automatic and non-waivable. Partnerships cannot be part of a Luxembourg fiscal unity (Article 164bis LIR), which requires a 95 percent holding in a corporate subsidiary. ATAD hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatch rules (law of 21 December 2018) apply mandatorily and no elective relief or hybrid neutrality option is available.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); prudential banking supervision is exercised concurrently by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); monetary policy and exchange-rate policy are delegated to the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control regime, no payment-licensing requirement for cross-border transfers, and no restriction on dividend, profit, or partnership-distribution remittance. Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Directive 88/361/EEC guarantee the free movement of capital; the only applicable obligations are prudential banking compliance, ECB balance-of-payments statistical reporting, and anti-money-laundering declarations. Profit distributions and capital-redemption proceeds of a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) are freely transferable to resident and non-resident partners in any currency without BCL approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may retain receipts in EUR or in any foreign currency in Luxembourg bank accounts without mandatory conversion. Export proceeds are subject to BCL/Eurosystem balance-of-payments statistical reporting via the instructing bank when the monthly reporting threshold for non-resident counterparties is exceeded; this is purely informational and does not restrict the use, holding, or onward disbursement of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EEA e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passported into Luxembourg under the Payment Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2); Low for non-EEA offshore digital banks and EMIs that lack a Luxembourg credit-institution, EMI, or payment-institution licence or an accepted EEA passport. Unlicensed offshore fintechs cannot lawfully maintain payment accounts in Luxembourg and would expose the SCSp treasury structure to regulatory and correspondent-banking integrity risk. Only EEA-authorized EMIs (e.g., licensed in Germany, Lithuania, or the Netherlands), or Luxembourg-regulated banks should support the SCSp's operational clearing and settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permissible under Luxembourg practice, and most banks accept secure video-identification for natural persons; for an SCSp, however, the general partner (GP), the registered agent, and any authorised signatory must expect a live due-diligence interview, held either physically at the bank or via an equivalent secure video conference, during account opening. Documentary trade (commercial Letters of Credit, guarantees, and trade loans) typically requires the signatory to complete an in-person or video interview before the facility is activated. A Luxembourg-registered professional support firm acting as registered agent is strongly recommended to satisfy the banks' substance and control checks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp partner opacity: the bank must identify all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) through the general partner and limited partners, including any partner residing in a high-risk jurisdiction, trust, or opaque holding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement (acte constitutif) and limited partnership agreement; RCSL registration extract dated within three months; UBO register filing confirmation (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); group-organisation chart tracing each GP and LP to natural-person UBOs using the CSSF-prescribed UBO declaration forms; certified passport copies and proof of residential address for all UBOs; tax-residence certificates for each corporate partner; source-of-funds documentation evidencing the initial capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the SCSp's declared wholesale-distribution purpose and the actual cross-border movement of goods and funds, especially round-tripping or high-value third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sales and purchase contracts with overseas distributors of pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base; commercial invoices and packing lists; customs declarations and forwarder bills of lading or airway bills; LCL/FCL shipment inventory ledger; Chamber of Commerce/RCSL activity certificate; tax adviser's written confirmation of the SCSp's default tax-transparent status or the opted taxable status; CFO/treasurer attestation of the commercial rationale for each flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classification risk: the bank may suspect the SCSp is operating as an unregulated collective investment undertaking requiring a CSSF Part II UCI authorisation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Operational business plan and budget proving active wholesale trading and distribution; payroll, storage, and logistics contracts evidencing substance; defined title-transfer and risk terms in the sales contracts; annual financial statements; legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat confirming that the SCSp is not a collective investment scheme within the meaning of the Luxembourg Law of 17 December 2010, as amended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargo, or trade-compliance flags on non-EU buyers or manufacturers of food commodities, requiring proof of end-user and goods characterisation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening results for all counterparties; certificate of origin for the hotpot soup base; quality and food-safety certificates (HACCP/ISO 22000); end-user declarations where the buyer operates in a high-risk or neighbouring sanctioned territory; letter of credit terms aligned with OFAC/EU-restricted-entity reviews; commercial invoice and Incoterms data supporting bonafide trade.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: a non-resident partner transfers EUR via SWIFT MT103 to the SCSp's EUR settlement account at a Luxembourg credit institution; Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – SCSP PARTNERSHIP' and may reference the applicable partnership agreement clause; for ECB balance-of-payments statistics the instructing bank codes the transaction as 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital'. Where the partner holds non-EUR funds, the correspondent bank applies a market-rate conversion; no BCL pre-authorisation is required. The receiving bank verifies the contributions evidence, including the partnership agreement, UBO declaration, and source-of-funds bank statements, before releasing funds from the capital escrow account; contributions in kind are supported by a notarised deed and independent valuation report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For open-account supplies: SWIFT MT103 from the SCSp's operational account to the supplier's account, with the invoice and contract references in Field 70 and supplier reference in Field 72; the bank reports the payment under the ECB balance-of-payments category 'Goods – General Merchandise on a BOP basis'. For documentary trade: commercial Letters of Credit issued by the buyer's bank and advised or confirmed through the SCSp's Luxembourg bank under SWIFT MT700, governed by UCP 600, with settlement at sight, deferred payment, or usance acceptance. Cross-border euro clearing occurs through T2 (successor to TARGET2) for ordinary RTGS payments and through T2S for instant payments if required; the bank handles the BCL statistical reporting on behalf of the SCSp.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards, OTC with the account bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and EMIR-compliant trade documentation
EUR/CNH (offshore renminbi) outright forwards and FX swaps, deliverable against CNH in Hong Kong or via an onshore renminbi trade-invoice-backed route where the bank's credit policy permits
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid currencies where the trade settlement currency is EUR and the fix is taken from a recognised reference rate
FX swaps (swap de change) matching the EUR capital injection into USD or CNH trade-disbursement legs, fully collateralised under a Credit Support Annex
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) for medium-term matching of foreign-currency disbursement exposures where the SCSp maintains a foreign-currency borrowing facility
Plain-vanilla FX options (purchase of EUR call / foreign currency put) offered under a bank-approved OTC derivative facility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review and, where triggered, event-driven update of the RCSL registration file and RESA publications (registered office, general partner, partnership agreement amendments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCSL) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual filing date for an SCSp; any change of registered particulars must be filed within one month of the event; an internal compliance audit should be completed within three months of each financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered astreinte (penalty payments), administrative fines up to EUR 10,000, and reiterated non-compliance may lead to judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCSL

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); the headline central CIT rate is 17%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent and not subject to corporate income tax at entity level; partner-level incentives include the Luxembourg IP/Nexus intellectual property box with 80% qualified income exemption, the research and development tax credit, investment tax credits, and the participation exemption. A standardized 5-year tax-loss horizon is used for directory risk-scoring; Luxembourg statutory law does not provide for loss carryback.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 530 – SCSp Transparency Return / ACD e-Tax module via MyGuichet; also Form 510 integrated partner-level income tax return for resident Luxembourg corporate partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the end of the SCSp fiscal year, unless extension is granted by the Administration des contributions directes; calendar-year taxpayers commonly file by 31 December of the following year in administrative practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, Luxembourg RCS registration number, registered office address, LEI, and full details of general and limited partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State each non-resident partner's country of tax residence, foreign tax identification number, TRC reference, and whether any Luxembourg permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B / Box 2 – Commercial profit and loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss derived from wholesale distribution of pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot soup base bricks, including revenue, cost of goods sold, warehousing, haulage, financing and overhead expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners without a Luxembourg PE should have no Luxembourg-source wholesale sales attributed; all resulting income is reported only in the residence state unless a PE threshold is triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C / Box 3 – Tax allocations to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership profit and loss allocated among general and limited partners in accordance with the SCSp agreement and Luxembourg tax transparency rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the allocable share of each non-resident partner; if attributable to a Luxembourg PE, complete the Luxembourg CIT and municipal business tax columns; otherwise mark 'no PE / not taxable in Luxembourg'.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D / Box 4 – Permanent establishment and municipal business tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of any Luxembourg fixed place of business through which the SCSp carries on hotpot soup base distribution, and computation of municipal business tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner is not subject to Luxembourg municipal business tax solely by reason of receiving a transparent share from a non-resident SCSp absent a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E / Box 5 – Cross-border payments and withholding statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of distributions, royalties, interest, service fees, and management charges paid to partners and connected parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide transaction-level information supporting arm's-length pricing and any claim to treaty relief or exemption from Luxembourg withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing interest accrues on any unpaid tax at 0.6% per month; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 may be imposed for failure to file a complete transparency return; deliberate concealment attracts tax fraud penalties and criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; distributions by an SCSp are not generally treated as dividends because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, and no Luxembourg withholding tax is levied on distribution proceeds paid to non-resident partners unless the profits are attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double tax treaty relief, the non-resident partner must: (1) obtain and submit a valid Luxembourg-formatted tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its residence country, (2) identify itself as the beneficial owner of the allocable income, (3) file a written reconciliation and refund claim with the ACD using the official administrative relief/refund procedure, and (4) demonstrate that the SCSp does not constitute a Luxembourg permanent establishment. The TRC must state the residence country, tax identification number, and taxable period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic withholding tax on outbound interest is 0%; Luxembourg domestic withholding tax on outbound royalties is 0%. Treaty rates are generally 0% for interest and royalties where applicable; no Luxembourg PE or substance abuse may otherwise limit treaty benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No separate Luxembourg statutory threshold requiring Local File or Master File at entity level; CbCR applies to groups with consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding EUR 750,000,000. ACD can require contemporaneous Local File in a tax audit. In all cases, arm's-length contemporaneous documentation for cross-border hotpot soup base distribution, tolling, procurement, and treasury transactions is mandatory in practice regardless of turnover.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate standalone Economic Substance Regulations in the form used by offshore financial centres, but the benefit of tax transparency, double tax treaty access, and preferential regimes is conditioned on real economic substance. The ACD applies the GAAR and anti-abuse principles under LIR Article 6 and OECD BEPS Action 6; the SCSp must demonstrate credible business purpose, premises, personnel, commercial risk, and decision-making in Luxembourg. Failure to do so may cause the SCSp to be recharacterized as a shell, ignored for tax purposes, or denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting the allocable share of taxable profit earned from pre-packaged hotpot soup base export distribution, manufacturing false invoices, backdating partner admission documents, or routing gross wholesale revenue through non-resident partners without Luxembourg PE substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty up to 100% of the evaded tax; late payment interest at 0.6% per month; fines up to EUR 100,000; criminal tax fraud prosecution with imprisonment up to five years under Luxembourg general tax procedure and criminal code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and any managing director of a corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes, penalties and interest when they knowingly signed false declarations or directed fraudulent distributions; courts may pierce the SCSp veil, order civil restitution, freeze personal assets, impose travel bans, and issue disqualification orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Tax Transparency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a nominee facade with no real office, no employees, no genuine economic risk, and no active management of the hotpot soup base supply chain; interposing the SCSp solely to avoid corporate income tax and Luxembourg municipal business tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the SCSp as taxable or subject to mandatory registration for corporate income tax; denial of the transparent partnership status; retroactive assessments of corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; penalty interest and fines; possible judicial dissolution as a sham enterprise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil-piercing attaches to the general partner, de facto managers, and knowing beneficial owners; they may be held personally liable for quantified tax deficiencies, loss of treaty benefits, and tort damages; travel restrictions and asset attachment orders may issue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Swift_TT or Letter of Credit payment rails to settle fictitious or overvalued hotpot soup base transactions, participating in trade-based money laundering, failing to conduct beneficial ownership and KYC identification, or circumventing export/sanctions restrictions on counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF-regulated professionals and the general partner face administrative fines and regulatory enforcement; violations of the Luxembourg anti-money laundering law and criminal code may result in fines up to EUR 1,250,000 or a fraction of turnover, asset confiscation, and imprisonment of five to ten years for organized money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers, beneficial owners, and directors who knowingly execute or permit layered trade payments bear personal criminal liability; Luxembourg courts may levy confiscation of personal assets, impose travel bans, and enforce extradition requests; wrongful concealment of beneficial ownership nullifies limited liability protection.
